title: Pala: an evening where poetry becomes performance
lead: A poem can live on a page. What happens when a performer brings it into a room full of listeners?

sections.title: Follow a voice into literature
sections.text: Jagannath Behera’s 2009 Akademi citation describes a performer who read literary classics across Odia, Bengali, Hindi, Sanskrit and English, drawing on them in performance. That is one artist’s recorded practice—a starting point for listening to the relationship between reading and the stage.

sections.title: An evening has many voices
sections.text: A report of the July 2012 Pala and Daskathia Utsav at Rabindra Mandap credits Santilata Sahu, Manorama Panda and Kumudini Patel among the performers. Their names invite further research into individual repertoires and artistic lives. A shared festival does not make Pala and Daskathia the same form.

sections.title: Find the poem behind the performance
sections.text: The Shree Jagannath Pala Research Foundation’s Pala Kabita catalogue offers a route into named texts and their credited authors. Begin with a title; then ask who performs it, which version they use, and what an unfamiliar listener should listen for.

sections.title: Plan to listen with care
sections.text: Ask a host or organiser about the actual performance, language, duration, seating and permission to photograph. No current event or troupe booking has been verified for this feature. A small introduction to the story may make an evening easier to follow.
